title: Parameter definition lexicon and violation classifier for tool/function JSON specs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: function/tool calling requires a single, well-understood JSON parameter schema surface that balances strict validation (safety & correctness) with compatibility for older SDKs and noisy user input. Current ticket space has many overlapping schemas and ad-hoc error messages which lead to poor developer UX and higher support volume.

Scope: define a compact, backwards-compatible lexicon for parameter definitions (human-friendly and machine-consumable), a deterministic violation classifier (error taxonomy + error codes), and a migration guide that runtime and SDK teams can adopt. This covers authoring conventions, runtime enforcement modes, telemetry points, and suggested error text templates for SDKs and Console UX.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a lightweight parameter-definition lexicon (PDL) that sits as a thin layer on top of JSON Schema. PDL fields: 'type' (string|number|boolean|object|array|enum|date), 'coerce' (none|trim|number|bool|iso_date), 'leniency' (strict|compat|permissive), 'examples' (list of values), 'ui_hint' (short-copy), 'min'/'max' for numeric/date, 'enum_values', 'pattern' (regex), and 'repair_hint' (suggested fix).

Validation modes implemented in runtime:
- strict: reject on any schema mismatch, return explicit error codes.
- compat: attempt safe coercions (according to 'coerce'), then validate; if coercion fails return classified error.
- permissive: best-effort normalize, attach 'validation_warnings' in response metadata but allow execution.

Violation classifier: canonical set of codes and buckets: PDL-001 MISSING_REQUIRED, PDL-002 TYPE_MISMATCH, PDL-003 ENUM_VIOLATION, PDL-004 OUT_OF_RANGE, PDL-005 PARSE_FAILURE, PDL-006 NORMALIZATION_APPLIED, PDL-007 AMBIGUOUS_PAYLOAD. Each code maps to: severity (error|warning|info), repair_hint, telemetry_key.

SDKs will expose standardized error objects: {code, message, field, provided, expected, repair_hint, docs_url}. Console will map codes to human-friendly help and quick-fix templates.

Back-compat policy: default to 'compat' for 30 days after rollout for pinned model versions; orgs can opt into 'strict' for new APIs or set 'per-route' enforcement.

Telemetry plan: emit 'param_validation.event' with tags {code, route, model_version, enforcement_mode, coercions_applied}. Use this to track repair_suggestion_acceptance_rate and customer-visible validation_fail_rate.
acceptance_criteria: PDL spec doc published in Drive with examples for common SDK languages
Runtime implements 'strict' and 'compat' enforcement modes and respects per-route override
Violation classifier enumerated with codes PDL-001..PDL-010 and mapping table published
SDK patch templates updated to return standardized error objects and include repair_hint
Integration tests: 20 representative functions with param variants showing expected errors/coercions
Telemetry dashboard surfaces param_validation_fail_rate and normalized repair_suggestion_acceptance_rate
decisions: Adopt PDL as a compatibility layer on top of JSON Schema rather than replacing existing schemas
Default enforcement mode for hosted API will be 'compat' for 30 days post-release to reduce breakage
Error objects use stable keys: code, message, field, provided, expected, repair_hint, docs_url
Do not attempt structural rewrites (e.g. rename keys) automatically; only type/coercion normalizations are permitted

error_mapping_examples: PDL-001 | MISSING_REQUIRED | field=\"user_email\" | message=\"Missing required parameter 'user_email'. Add a valid email or set 'leniency' to permissive for relaxed enforcement.\" | repair_hint=\"add 'user_email' in payload\"
PDL-002 | TYPE_MISMATCH | field=\"limit\" | message=\"Expected integer for 'limit' but received 'ten'. Suggestion: use numeric value or enable coercion.\" | repair_hint=\"convert to integer\"
PDL-003 | ENUM_VIOLATION | field=\"mode\" | message=\"Value 'fastish' not in allowed set [\"fast\", \"slow\"].\" | repair_hint=\"choose from allowed enum values\"
PDL-006 | NORMALIZATION_APPLIED | field=\"date\" | message=\"Input '3/4/25' normalized to '2025-03-04' using iso_date coercion.\" | repair_hint=\"none (info)\"
